quote.q: तत्र यदा शब्दरूपे विधीयेते तदा सर्वस्येति स्थानषष्ठीयं सम्पद्यते; अनियतसम्बन्धत्वात्? <<षष्ठी स्थानेयोगा>> [[1.1.49]]  इति न्यायात्

अत्र ठा दशभ्यः संख्याः संख्येये वर्तन्तेऽ इति'द्वे'  इत्यस्य संख्येयापेक्षायां शब्दानुशासनप्रस्तावाच्छब्दरूपे संख्येये'षष्ठी स्थानेयोगा'  इति वचनात्सर्वस्येति स्थानषष्ठी, सर्वस्य पर्यादेः स्थाने द्वे शब्दरूपे भवत इत्यर्थः, यथा - ठस्तेर्भूःऽ इति, तदा'स्थाने द्विर्वचनम्'  इत्ययं पक्षो भवति

paribhashas.effect: named here, not applied — Bhāṣya: सर्वस्य is said so that 1.1.52 does NOT apply (“अलोऽन्त्यनिवृत्त्यर्थम्”); doubling is not a substitution anyway.

अलोऽन्त्यस्य विधयो भवन्तीत्यन्त्यस्य द्विर्वचनं मा भूदिति

why.txt: आदेशाः is simply the commentary's standing name for the class of substitutes (वाम्, नौ, त्वा, मा, ते, मे, etc.) taught a few rules earlier, used here as their collective label rather than a word fetched by anuवृत्ति. — बालमनोरमा: “वां-नावाद्यादेशा अनन्वादेशे पाक्षिकाः”

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)
a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to) — प्रथमान्तात् — a word ENDING in that case ending

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

यदि स्यात्'संयोगान्तस्य लोपः'  इत्यत्र'षष्ठी स्थानेयोगा इत्येतस्याभावातच्छेषस्य ठलो

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”) — व्रश्च भ्रस्ज सृज मृज यज राज भ्राज च्छ शकारान्तानाम् — what ENDS in it, as the Kāśikā reads it

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). this rule is in the tripādī: for every rule before it, it counts as not having applied — काशिका on 8.2.1: “इत उत्तरं चोत्तर उत्तरो योगः पूर्वत्रपूर्वत्रासिद्धो भवति, असिद्धवद् भवति। सिद्धकार्यं न करोतीत्यर्थः”

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: When one sound is taught in place of a longer item named in the 6th case, it replaces only that item's last sound. Not when the place is itself one sound or a position (उपधा, टि), not for augments, and not for लुक् — the whole suffix goes. (Nyāsa: “आदेशः पुनरत्रैकाल्लभ्यते।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

names what FOLLOWS — the replacement is of what precedes it

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

q: the part of which word is replaced?

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

left.txt: this rule is in the tripādī: for every rule before it, it counts as not having applied — काशिका on 8.2.1: “इत उत्तरं चोत्तर उत्तरो योगः पूर्वत्रपूर्वत्रासिद्धो भवति, असिद्धवद् भवति। सिद्धकार्यं न करोतीत्यर्थः”

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). why.txt: वन here means the word वन itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
it describes another word of the rule

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
it describes another word of the rule

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”
the substitute chosen is the NEAREST in articulation — each sound is replaced by the NEAREST sound of the group (sound for sound)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
